newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola Enterprises sees dilution in '97.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola Enterprises sees dilution in '97.

text.p: Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc said on Wednesday that based on current marketing plans and a competitive environment, it expects the dilution from its British, French, and Belgian acquisitions to be about $0.05 a share for 1997.
Coca-Cola Enterprises reported a fourth quarter profit of $0.06 a share, compared with a loss of $0.03 a share for the previous fourth quarter.
According to the company, the results of the French and Belgian operations reduced fourth quarter 1996 net income by slightly more than $0.05 per share.
The company said that this fourth-quarter dilution is driven by seasonally low winter carbonated beverage consumption in Europe and fixed costs such as depreciation, amortization, and interest.
Coca-Cola Enterprises said it expects that the seasonal dilution from the French and Belgian operations will continue in the first and fourth quarters of 1997 and for the foreseeable future.
The seasonal dilution will become more pronounced once the company completes the pending acquisition of the Coca-Cola and Cadbury bottling operations in Great Britain, the company said.
Under favorable market and weather conditions, these European acquisitions should be additive to the company's results in the second and third quarters, it said.
